title: Single-encoding video streams are severely throttled by index-based simulcast mapping
test: A browser probe (results/check-10-probe.cjs.txt; output in check-10-probe-output.json). It runs the real app, built with vite into the scratchpad, against the real server.js (NEXTRA_SMOKE_TEST=1, ports from claimServerPorts) in Playwright Chromium 153 and Firefox 155. The Playwright lock was held. It hooks RTCPeerConnection.prototype.addTransceiver, starts sharing a stubbed 1280x720 capture, switches the live profile 1440p/60 -> 1080p/30 -> 4K/60, and reads the producer sender's getParameters().encodings after each step. A second check (results/check-10-unit.cjs.txt) slices the unchanged getSimulcastEncodings and applyProducerBitrateProfile out of src/HostView.jsx, at HEAD and at ac1c688, and runs them against fake senders with 3 encodings and with 1.
proof: The claim does not hold. Its premise, a video sender with only one encoding, never happens in Nextra. The only video produce() call (src/HostView.jsx:1500-1504) always passes getSimulcastEncodings(), i.e. [r0, r1, r2]. The mediasoup-client 3.24.5 handlers (Chrome111.js:240-265, Firefox120.js:254-268, Safari12.js:241-266) give each one rid r${idx} and pass them in that order to addTransceiver's sendEncodings, without reordering. mediasoup-client's own setMaxSpatialLayer (Chrome111.js:459-468) maps encodings by index on the same assumption. In the probe, both browsers kept 3 encodings in order rid r0, r1, r2, and after every profile change each one held its own rid's target. For example, at 1440p/60: [0] r0 2520000, [1] r1 8400000, [2] r2 21000000. At 4K/60: 4320000, 14400000, 36000000. So nothing was capped at the r0 share. Even in the hypothetical case: a browser that cannot simulcast trims sendEncodings from the tail (webrtc-pc addTransceiver, maxN), and an answer that rejects simulcast keeps the first encoding. Either way the lone encoding left is the requested r0, already at scaleResolutionDownBy 4 and the r0 cap from produce() itself. The unit check shows applyProducerBitrateProfile leaves it at that same value ({scaleResolutionDownBy:4,maxBitrate:2520000} in and out), so this function would not be the cause. The defect was not real on the original code either. The function is identical at ac1c688 and has not changed since 4fa0eef (2026-03-26), which added it together with the simulcast produce() call. ac1c688's lockfile has the same mediasoup-client 3.24.5, and the unit check gives the same output on ac1c688's HostView.jsx. No file changed and nothing was committed.
